sample_size.notes: Sample covers 4 variants (UA/UD x Bull/Bear). Ascending scallop has a rising left side.

target_calculation.description: Compute scallop height (peak - start); project from breakout point in breakout direction.

ultimate_high_method.definition: Highest price after upward breakout before 20% reversal

ultimate_low_method.definition: Lowest price after downward breakout before 20% reversal

failure_definition.description: Break-even failure: price fails to move 5% in breakout direction.

post_breakout_measurement.lookahead_note: Median ~68 days. Wide range: bull/UA longest (162), bear/UD shortest (35). Use per-variant if available.

performance_statistics.worst_performer: bull/UD (27% BE failure — descending breakout in bull market is unreliable)

notes: PDF source: Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (2nd ed.), chapter 38, p647-676.
Legacy digitized file scallop_ascending_descending_digitized.json groups all 4 scallop variants together with NO failure_rate / sample_size / target — this file fills that gap for Ascending variants.
Critical: bull/UD (downward breakout in bull market) has 27% BE failure — very unreliable. Most other variants are continuation (UA) and reliable.
Ascending scallop's J-shape has the OPENING on the lower-left, HANDLE on the upper-right.
